head: working-tree
subject: gRPC xDS initial resource timers
change: runtime.Options.resource_timer_is_transient_error implements the gRPC xDS server feature of the same name together with the initial resource-fetch timer. Controller.nextResourceTimerExpiry and pollResourceTimers arm a timer for every subscribed but undelivered LDS/RDS/CDS/EDS/SDS resource, and resourceStatus reports requested, acked, does_not_exist or timeout. The default budget is 15 s, or 30 s with the feature; an expired timer reports does_not_exist, or a transient timeout with the feature, matching grpc-core's ResourceState. Delivery clears the timer. Options.resource_timer_timeout may shorten the budget.

tests.unit: src/grpc/xds/runtime/resource_timer_tests.zig covers the delta and SotW clients: requested to does_not_exist without the feature, requested to timeout with it, delivery clearing the listener timer while the referenced CDS stays pending, and an EDS timer expiring independently next to an acked cluster.

focused_gate.command: zig build test-lib -Dtest-filter='resource timer' -Dtest-filter='xDS runtime' --summary all

notes: The timer follows grpc-core's per-resource ResourceState: it only arms for a subscribed resource that has never been cached, and a timed-out resource stays subscribed so a later delivery still applies. netz exposes the outcome through resourceStatus; cached configuration is unchanged because the timed-out resource was never cached. Callers drive the timer with nextResourceTimerExpiry or pollResourceTimers after each discovery step so newly desired names are registered.
